name: Charles III
role: King of the United Kingdom and the other Commonwealth realms (since 2022); Prince of Wales 1958-2022
summary: Charles III is a constitutional monarch who, as Prince of Wales, publicly campaigned on organic and sustainable farming, climate and nature, traditional architecture and urbanism, integrated medicine and interfaith understanding. His own speeches combine a precautionary, spiritually grounded environmentalism with respect for tradition and heritage, support for diversity, and market-based climate action led by the private sector. As king he is constitutionally neutral and says he will not campaign, so his recorded views come mainly from his earlier speeches and letters.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Mixed: in Harmony (Nature chapter, 'Economics') he calls the pricing of ecosystems at zero a market failure of epic proportions, yet he also backs market incentives and private-sector mobilisation (Foundations chapter; COP26 address 2021 asking for clear market signals).

regulate-corporations.rationale: In Harmony (Foundations chapter) he says governments' tax, procurement and research policy and 'well-targeted incentives or disincentives' are needed to move companies to sustainability; at COP26 he asked for clear market signals agreed globally. He mostly urges voluntary corporate reporting, so support for tighter regulation is only partly stated.

decide-locally.rationale: Said communities have the best answers if engaged and pledged consultation with local people on architecture and rural housing.

more-religion-public.rationale: Criticised secularisation and 'cynical secularism' and called for the sacred traditions to be returned to the mainstream of thinking; did not propose specific legal roles.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: At CHOGM 2022 expressed sorrow at slavery and said the Commonwealth must find new ways to acknowledge its past; did not set out a programme of action.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Urged national pride in British values and culture; his record includes heritage building restoration and promotion of traditional architecture.

gradual-change.rationale: Stresses learning from the past and evolving tradition ('tending the fire, not the ashes'), and warns that anything not 'modern' is dismissed; no explicit statement on pace of social change.

free-trade.rationale: Rejected the view that GATT globalisation of agricultural trade would be wholly beneficial; said globalisation brings advantages but also dangers, notably for poorer people and traditional cultures.

limit-growth.rationale: Argued that continuous economic growth on finite resources 'does not work out' and that consumption must fall; elsewhere he backs 'sustainable growth', so the support is for limits on current growth, not for ending it.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Called climate change the greatest threat humanity has faced and urged a war-like footing and radical transformation of the economy at Davos and COP26.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Said environmental problems cannot be solved by ever more technology alone ('fixing the pump and not the well') and that science and technology cannot supply what is missing.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Harmony (Foundations chapter) says government decisions on tax, procurement, research spending and market incentives can steer the economy toward sustainability and cites more national income being invested in renewable infrastructure.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Spoke for smallholders and family farms over concentrated agribusiness; his record is on farmland, not property generally.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: No stated position found: holding the throne by inheritance is his role, not an argument for it, and he is not recorded arguing the principle.

separate-church-state.rationale: As Prince and King he has kept the Sovereign's role in the Church of England: his 2022 accession address calls the Church 'my own faith so deeply rooted' and acknowledges the Sovereign's special responsibility to it, and in 2015 he said he would keep the title Defender of the Faith. He also wants other faiths protected.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Harmony (Relationship chapter, 'Playing a part') says the most effective response to Amazon deforestation has been the transfer of control to indigenous people, who see the forest as their home and heritage, and praises their stewardship.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Harmony (Foundations chapter) says the values-free education of the West fosters an excessive personal focus and the belief that things will work out if everybody looks after themselves, and that unselfish people are happier.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Harmony (Nature chapter, 'Economics') notes approvingly a UNDP finding that people should recognise responsibility and says modern thinking has made rights more important than responsibility; the closing chapter regrets 'rights' without duty.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Said we need to rediscover reverence for the natural world 'irrespective of its usefulness to ourselves'.

limit-population.rationale: Harmony (Nature chapter 'Economics'; Foundations chapter) says population growth has to be part of the debate and that we must address how to 'stabilize and even reduce' the human population, asking faith and political leaders to consider family size.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Mixed: Harmony (Harmony and Nature chapters) says industrial development has put 'us on a very wrong road' and is ecologically destructive, but also acknowledges large benefits in health care and material comfort and says technology is still needed.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Urged using science to understand nature rather than change it and warned against treating the world as a laboratory; supports innovation for climate but not speed at the cost of institutions.

restore-past-order.rationale: Mixed: Harmony (Golden Thread and Age of Disconnection chapters) argues the West abandoned traditional wisdom and should reintegrate it, but he says ancient societies were cruel by modern standards and calls for combining tradition with the best of modern knowledge.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Harmony (Renaissance chapter) says he is absolutely not saying we do not need technology and wants traditional wisdom reintegrated with modern knowledge; he admires indigenous societies without proposing a return to their way of life.

universal-morality.rationale: Harmony (Golden Thread chapter) speaks of an 'eternal law' and universal justice and the common good grounded in nature's order, but he stresses intuition and spiritual perception more than reason.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Said neither rational analysis nor intuition is much use alone, criticised the dominance of scientific rationalism and urged recovery of the sacred and 'wisdom of the heart'.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Championed conserving historic buildings and townscapes, opposed towers in historic skylines, and funded rescues such as Dumfries House and Middleport Pottery.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Seeks integration of minority faith communities through 'unity through diversity' and supports minority self-esteem and identity, not giving up their culture.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Harmony (closing chapter) calls for replacing the obsession with unlimited growth and competition with a quest for well-being and cooperation.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Harmony (Foundations chapter) says the poorest carry the cost of lost natural resilience and that ending poverty is essential; he backs microfinance and community banking for the poor.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Said 'our diversity is our greatest strength' and advocates 'unity through diversity' and fairness for minority communities.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Said economic development and related global problems need a moral, unselfish response and praised aid NGOs and government-NGO partnership.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Argued repeatedly that a precautionary approach is a sign of strength and wisdom, and criticised ignoring it on genetic modification and climate.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Said of the transition to sovereign 'I do realise that it is a separate exercise... I understand entirely how that should operate' and has always said he is not party political.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Championed the Commonwealth and British cultural diplomacy (British Council, BBC World Service) as ways of projecting British influence abroad.

elective-rulers.rationale: No stated position found: holding the throne by inheritance is his role, not an argument for it, and he is not recorded arguing the principle.

parliament-supreme.rationale: His 2022 accession address pledges to uphold the constitutional principles of the nation and honours the precious traditions, freedoms and responsibilities of the parliamentary system.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Criticised treating animals as machines in industrial farming and 'the treatment meted out to animals in factory farms'.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Farms livestock organically while condemning factory-farm treatment, showing support for humane use rather than rejecting animal use.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Founded the Prince's Trust in 1976 and lent his name to hundreds of charities for disadvantaged people; the record shows a duty-of-service view rather than a stated principle.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Harmony (Age of Disconnection chapter, 'Keeping the voters happy') says consumerism was engineered through advertising so that desire is never fulfilled, which keeps the population becalmed.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Said consumerism and the hunger for ever more things harms the Earth and creates unhappiness; urged the world to reduce its desire to consume.

local-production.rationale: Convened work on a 'much more local model of food production and distribution' and urged buying British produce.

religion-illusion.rationale: Harmony (Harmony and closing chapters) treats faith and the sacred traditions as carrying real meaning and insight, and rejects the material-only view that dismisses them.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Commissioned portraits of seven Holocaust survivors; no direct statement found.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: As King undertook his first official engagement for the LGBT+ community, unveiling the national memorial for LGBT armed forces veterans; no direct statement found.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Harmony (Renaissance chapter) argues planning should be done with communities rather than for them and describes his Enquiry by Design method for community decision-making; the evidence concerns local planning rather than politics generally.

islam-incompatible.rationale: In 1993 argued that Western prejudice about Islam is mistaken and that what binds the two worlds is more powerful than what divides them.

dynastic-succession.rationale: No stated position found: holding the throne by inheritance is his role, not an argument for it, and he is not recorded arguing the principle.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Argued that humans have a spiritual essence and that policy, economics and science neglect it; said the sacred should shape sustainable development.

gm-crops.rationale: Said it is not right to tamper with the building blocks of life and called genetically modified crops unproven; spoke against them in 1996, 1998 and 2000.

dense-cities.rationale: Harmony (Renaissance chapter) contrasts the wasteful suburban model with integrated, compact design and describes Poundbury as high-density, mixed-use and walkable; the case is made mainly on community and space-saving grounds.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Has long urged the 'polluter pays' principle and proper use of taxes, policy and regulation to make sustainable options pay; also supports regulation, so not a pure tax-over-regulation position.

future-generations.rationale: Repeatedly framed stewardship as a duty to hand the Earth on to future generations; spoke of a sacred trust.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Calls for restoring and valuing natural capital and putting a value on carbon; says nature's capital underpins economic capital.

religions-one-truth.rationale: In 1994 he said disputes over the interpretation of faith are a waste since 'we are all actually aiming for the same ultimate goal'; spoke of a common monotheistic vision and of all sacred traditions.

farm-price-support.rationale: Wrote to Blair in 2004 that 'every support must be given to beef farmers' if subsidies are withdrawn and backed CAP reform paying farmers for environmental management.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Cited as a mark of a non-mediaeval society that Muslim women's rights to property, inheritance and business were set down in the Qur'an and are valuable.

women-suffrage.rationale: Cited with approval that Islamic countries gave women the vote as early as Europe and that women are not automatically second-class citizens.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Harmony (Harmony chapter) criticises fundamentalist religion in both Christianity and Islam, saying the more puritanical and literal the reading, the more a culture abandons its symbolic traditions and replaces mystery with a vain search for certainty.

national-church-status.rationale: His 2022 accession address acknowledges the Sovereign's special relationship and responsibility toward the Church of England, but he has also said he wants to protect all faiths (1994: 'defender of faith'; 2022: society of many faiths), so the evidence is mixed.

simple-living.rationale: Harmony (Nature chapter) endorses Gandhi's point that Western life lacks a sense of limit and calls for a culture rooted in fulfilment rather than consumption; he does not call for self-sufficient living, so this is partial.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Harmony (Harmony chapter) states his aim of reintegrating traditional wisdom with the best of what we can do now, and Renaissance chapter on architecture combines traditional design with modern technology.

notes:
Living person: no inferences from his role or title; answers are from speeches and record. As king he is constitutionally neutral, and in 2018 said that being sovereign is 'a separate exercise' from his earlier campaigning, so statements as Prince of Wales are treated as his record. The King's Speeches state the government's programme and were not used. Full texts of his books (Harmony, A Vision of Britain) and the black spider letters were not available to download; only reporting on the letters (CNN) was used. The Britain in the World speech is undated on its page; its content points to the 1990s. Criminalize-homosexuality and holocaust-denial answers rest on record (a memorial he unveiled, portraits he commissioned) rather than a stated position.

Merged with an independent claude-sonnet-5-5 audit: 26 answers taken from it, 29 agreed, 0 conflicts settled by the integrator.

claude-sonnet-5-5 notes: Most answers rest on Harmony (2010) and his climate speeches; as King he is bound by convention not to take party-political positions, so formal assent to laws is not counted. His views on many ordinary left-right issues (taxation, welfare, abortion, same-sex marriage, immigration) are not recorded in his own words and are left null.
